idioms.meaning: Easy wins that require minimal effort
idioms.example: Let's tackle the low-hanging fruit first — onboarding copy fixes will boost activation today.

idioms.meaning: Make a significant measurable impact
idioms.example: Adding dark mode won't move the needle — focus on the retention loop.

idioms.meaning: Make a decisive action or final commitment
idioms.example: We've tested enough — time to pull the trigger on the Stripe integration.

idioms.meaning: Release the product or feature to users
idioms.example: It's 80% there and users need it now — just ship it.

idioms.meaning: Signs clearly indicate what will happen
idioms.example: The writing's on the wall — if churn stays at 15%, we're dead in 6 months.

idioms.meaning: Attempt something impossibly ambitious
idioms.example: Don't boil the ocean with an AI feature set — start with one use case.

idioms.meaning: Blindly believe in something without questioning
idioms.example: Don't drink the Kool-Aid on every YC trend — validate with your own users.

idioms.meaning: Launch a product commercially for the first time
idioms.example: Our go-to-market strategy is content-led — zero paid ads until PMF.

idioms.meaning: Earning just enough revenue to cover basic living costs
idioms.example: We hit ramen profitable at $2K MRR — enough to skip the fundraising circus.

idioms.meaning: Sudden exponential growth after a flat period
idioms.example: Month 8 hit hockey stick growth — word of mouth finally kicked in.

idioms.meaning: Aggressively capture market share before competitors
idioms.example: AI content tools are in land-grab mode — first to nail creator UX wins.

idioms.meaning: Create a sustainable competitive advantage
idioms.example: Our data flywheel is the moat — every user makes the AI smarter for all.

idioms.meaning: Competing primarily by lowering prices unsustainably
idioms.example: Competing on price is a race to the bottom — differentiate on workflow.

idioms.meaning: The minimum requirements to compete
idioms.example: Mobile support is table stakes now — not a feature, a baseline.

idioms.meaning: Product-market fit — when a product satisfies strong market demand
idioms.example: You know you have PMF when users complain about downtime instead of features.

idioms.phrase: hit the nail on the head
idioms.meaning: Describe exactly what is right or true
idioms.example: You hit the nail on the head — the real problem is onboarding, not pricing.

idioms.meaning: Return to the starting point after a setback
idioms.example: The API migration failed, so we're back to square one.

idioms.meaning: Get to the point without wasting time
idioms.example: Let me cut to the chase — we need $5K MRR by September or we pivot.

idioms.meaning: Having shared understanding or agreement
idioms.example: Before we build, let's get on the same page about the user persona.

idioms.meaning: Fail to follow through on a responsibility
idioms.example: I dropped the ball on the email sequence — zero follow-ups went out.

idioms.meaning: A practical guideline based on experience, not exact science
idioms.example: Rule of thumb: if the feature takes more than a week, split it.

idioms.meaning: An obvious problem no one wants to discuss
idioms.example: The elephant in the room is that our free tier cannibalizes paid.

idioms.meaning: Set a higher standard
idioms.example: Notion raised the bar for documentation UX — we need to match it.

idioms.meaning: Do something in a cheaper or easier way, sacrificing quality
idioms.example: We cut corners on testing and it cost us a full day of downtime.

idioms.meaning: Changing the criteria for success unfairly
idioms.example: The investor keeps moving the goalposts — first ARR, now cohort retention.

idioms.meaning: Destroy relationships permanently through actions
idioms.example: Don't burn bridges with your co-founder — the startup world is small.

idioms.meaning: Making the important decisions
idioms.example: As a solo founder, you're calling the shots — own every outcome.

idioms.meaning: Return to discuss something later
idioms.example: Let's circle back on the pricing page after we see this week's data.

idioms.meaning: An extremely easy decision
idioms.example: At $10/month for unlimited AI calls, it's a no-brainer for creators.

idioms.meaning: Give up or admit defeat
idioms.example: Three pivots in, most founders would throw in the towel — we kept going.

idioms.meaning: Personal stake or risk in the outcome
idioms.example: Advisors without skin in the game give generic advice — give them equity.

idioms.meaning: Executing with high speed and urgency
idioms.example: We're moving fast — shipping weekly, measuring daily, iterating hourly.

idioms.meaning: Embrace a challenge or opportunity with full commitment
idioms.example: The AI hype is real — lean in now while distribution is cheap.

idioms.meaning: Focus on your area of expertise, don't overreach
idioms.example: I stay in my lane — product and growth. Legal goes to the lawyer.

idioms.meaning: Handle multiple different roles or responsibilities
idioms.example: Solo founders wear many hats — I'm the dev, designer, and support team.

idioms.meaning: Share confidential or internal information transparently
idioms.example: We opened the kimono on our metrics — full transparency builds trust.

idioms.meaning: Unconventional or less commonly taken approach
idioms.example: Our distribution strategy is off the beaten path — no ads, pure community.

idioms.meaning: More advanced or innovative than others
idioms.example: Building AI tools in 2024 put us ahead of the curve for the creator wave.

idioms.meaning: In a difficult or disadvantaged position
idioms.example: Missing the Product Hunt launch put us behind the eight ball on visibility.

idioms.meaning: A goal or requirement that keeps changing
idioms.example: User expectations for AI quality are a moving target — ship fast, adapt faster.

idioms.meaning: Deeply involved in details, potentially losing the big picture
idioms.example: I got in the weeds with CSS tweaks — should've focused on conversion.

idioms.meaning: Make conditions equal for everyone
idioms.example: AI tools level the playing field — a solo creator can compete with agencies.

idioms.meaning: Doubt or reconsider a decision after making it
idioms.example: Don't second-guess the pricing change — the data supports it.

idioms.meaning: Act or speak impulsively without careful thought
idioms.example: I shot from the hip on that tweet and it went viral — sometimes instinct works.

idioms.meaning: Act tough and uncompromising in negotiations
idioms.example: The enterprise client tried to play hardball on pricing — we held firm.
